This approach enables more realistic video synthesis with improved physical consistency, such as accurate collisions and material responses.

case_studies.abstract: Transformer models are widely deployed in critical AI applications, yet faults in their attention mechanisms, projections, and other internal components often degrade behavior silently without raising runtime errors. Existing fault diagnosis techniques often target generic deep neural networks and cannot identify which transformer component is responsible for an observed symptom. case_studies.summary: Transformer models are widely used in critical AI applications, but faults in their internal components can silently degrade their behavior, and existing fault diagnosis techniques often cannot identify the responsible component. DEFault++ is a hierarchical learning-based diagnostic technique that detects, categorizes, and diagnoses faults in transformer architectures at three levels of abstraction. The technique classifies faults into one of 12 transformer-specific categories, enabling targeted corrections and improved model reliability.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the DEFault++ technique by integrating it into their model development pipelines to detect and diagnose faults early on, reducing the risk of silent failures and improving overall model performance. By using a hierarchical learning-based approach, practitioners can develop more robust and reliable transformer models that can operate effectively in critical applications.

The outcome of this approach is a significant improvement in DSM modularization, with potential applications in various engineering design fields.

case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) make reward design in reinforcement learning substantially more scalable, but generated rewards are not automatically reliable training objectives. case_studies.summary: The problem of unreliable reward hypotheses generated by large language models (LLMs) in reinforcement learning is addressed by proposing a competence-aware verification and phase-aware deployment approach. The AI approach, RHyVE, treats generated rewards as reward hypotheses whose utility depends on the competence of the current policy and the phase of training. The outcome is a more effective and reliable method for deploying LLM-generated reward hypotheses in reinforcement learning.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the RHyVE approach by first assessing the competence of their current policy and the phase of training, and then using this information to selectively deploy and verify LLM-generated reward hypotheses. case_studies.summary: The problem of equilibrium concepts in game theory is that they often only guarantee stability against unilateral deviations, leaving them vulnerable to coordinated deviations by coalitions. The authors propose an alternative solution concept that minimizes coalitional deviation incentives, providing a more robust equilibrium concept. This approach has the potential to improve the stability of multi-agent systems, but its practical applications and outcomes are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore the use of optimization techniques to minimize coalitional deviation incentives in their own multi-agent systems. By doing so, they can develop more robust and stable systems that can withstand coordinated deviations by coalitions.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of more stable and robust multi-agent systems, which can be applied to various industries such as finance or transportation. Companies can leverage this concept to create more reliable and efficient systems, leading to increased productivity and competitiveness.

case_studies.title: Splitting Argumentation Frameworks with Collective Attacks and Supports
case_studies.abstract: This work proposes novel splitting techniques for argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. We base our studies on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs) which generalize argumentation frameworks with collective attacks (SETAFs), as well as bipolar argumentation frameworks (BAFs), by incorporating both collective attacks and supports. Notably, BSAFs establish a crucial link to structured argumentation as they naturally capture general (potentially non-flat) assumption-based argumentation. The increase in expressiveness calls for diverse forms o
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the need for novel splitting techniques in argumentation formalisms that incorporate supports between defeasible elements. The AI approach proposed is based on bipolar set-based argumentation frameworks (BSAFs), which generalize argumentation frameworks with collective attacks and supports. The outcome of this study is a crucial link to structured argumentation, naturally capturing general assumption-based argumentation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilize BSAFs to model complex argumentation scenarios, incorporating both collective attacks and supports. By doing so, they can develop more expressive and nuanced argumentation systems, capable of capturing a wider range of real-world scenarios.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this research is the development of advanced argumentation-based decision support systems, which can be applied in various domains such as law, medicine, or finance. These systems can provide more accurate and informative decision-making outcomes, leading to increased efficiency and effectiveness in these fields.

case_studies.title: SpecVQA: A Benchmark for Spectral Understanding and Visual Question Answering in Scientific Images
case_studies.abstract: Spectra are a prevalent yet highly information-dense form of scientific imagery, presenting substantial challenges to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) due to their unstructured and domain-specific characteristics. Here we introduce SpecVQA, a professional scientific-image benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on scientific spectral understanding, covering 7 representative spectrum types with expert-annotated question-answer pairs. The aim comprises two aspects: spectra scientific QA evaluation and corresponding underlying task evaluation. SpecVQA contains 620 figures and 3100 QA p
case_studies.summary: The SpecVQA benchmark addresses the challenge of evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on scientific spectral understanding, a prevalent yet information-dense form of scientific imagery. The AI approach involves creating a professional scientific-image benchmark with expert-annotated question-answer pairs to assess multimodal models. The outcome is a comprehensive evaluation of MLLMs' abilities in scientific spectral understanding, covering 7 representative spectrum types with 620 figures and 3100 QA pairs.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the SpecVQA benchmark to evaluate and improve their multimodal models' performance on scientific spectral understanding, enabling more accurate analysis of scientific images. By leveraging the SpecVQA dataset, developers can fine-tune their models to better handle unstructured and domain-specific characteristics of scientific spectra.
case_studies.monetisation: The SpecVQA benchmark presents a potential business opportunity for companies developing AI-powered analysis tools for scientific research, particularly in fields relying heavily on spectral analysis, such as materials science or pharmaceuticals. By integrating the SpecVQA benchmark into their products, these companies can demonstrate the effectiveness of their AI models in real-world scientific applications, increasing their market competitiveness.

case_studies.title: Graph World Models: Concepts, Taxonomy, and Future Directions
case_studies.abstract: As one of the mainstream models of artificial intelligence, world models allow agents to learn the representation of the environment for efficient prediction and planning. However, classical world models based on flat tensors face several key problems, including noise sensitivity, error accumulation and weak reasoning. To address these limitations, many recent studies use graph structure to decompose the environment into entity nodes and interactive edges, and model virtual environments in a structured space. This paper systematically formalizes and unifies these emerging graph-based works und
case_studies.summary: Classical world models face limitations such as noise sensitivity and weak reasoning, which can be addressed by using graph structures to decompose the environment into entity nodes and interactive edges. The proposed approach, Graph World Models, systematically formalizes and unifies emerging graph-based works to model virtual environments in a structured space. This approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of prediction and planning in artificial intelligence agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by incorporating graph structures into their world models to improve robustness and reasoning capabilities. To implement this, they can use graph-based algorithms and techniques, such as graph neural networks, to model complex environments and relationships.
case_studies.monetisation: The Graph World Models approach has potential applications in areas such as robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart cities, where accurate prediction and planning are critical. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more efficient and effective AI systems, such as autonomous navigation systems or smart home devices, which can be marketed and sold to consumers.

case_studies.title: SecMate: Multi-Agent Adaptive Cybersecurity Troubleshooting with Tri-Context Personalization
case_studies.abstract: Recent advances in large language models and agentic frameworks have enabled virtual customer assistants (VCAs) for complex support. We present SecMate, a multi-agent VCA for cybersecurity troubleshooting that integrates device, user, and service specificity from conversational and device-level signals. Device specificity is provided by a lightweight local diagnostic utility, while user specificity relies on implicit proficiency inference and profile-aware troubleshooting. Service specificity is achieved through a proactive, context-aware recommender. We evaluate SecMate in a controlled study
case_studies.summary: The problem of cybersecurity troubleshooting is addressed through the development of SecMate, a multi-agent virtual customer assistant that integrates device, user, and service specificity. SecMate uses a combination of conversational and device-level signals, including a lightweight local diagnostic utility and implicit proficiency inference, to provide personalized troubleshooting. The outcome of this approach is a more effective and efficient cybersecurity troubleshooting process.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons of SecMate by incorporating multi-agent architectures and tri-context personalization into their own virtual customer assistant systems. By leveraging device, user, and service specificity, practitioners can create more effective and efficient troubleshooting systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of SecMate presents a clear business opportunity for companies looking to provide advanced cybersecurity troubleshooting solutions. By commercializing SecMate, companies can offer a unique and effective product that addresses the growing need for personalized cybersecurity support.

case_studies.title: Benchmarking Complex Multimodal Document Processing Pipelines: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Enterprise AI
case_studies.abstract: Most enterprise document AI today is a pipeline. Parse, index, retrieve, generate. Each of those stages has been studied to death on its own -- what's still hard is evaluating the system as a whole. We built EnterpriseDocBench to take a swing at it: parsing fidelity, indexing efficiency, retrieval relevance, and generation groundedness, all on the same corpus. The corpus is built from public, permissively licensed documents across six enterprise domains (five represented in the current pilot). We ran three pipelines through it -- BM25, dense embedding, and a hybrid -- all with the same GPT-5 g
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating complex multimodal document processing pipelines is addressed through the creation of a unified evaluation framework. The AI approach involves building EnterpriseDocBench, a corpus of public documents across six enterprise domains, to test parsing fidelity, indexing efficiency, retrieval relevance, and generation groundedness. The outcome is a benchmarking framework that can be used to assess the performance of different document processing pipelines.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this framework, AI practitioners can use EnterpriseDocBench to evaluate the performance of their own document processing pipelines and identify areas for improvement. By using a standardized benchmarking framework, practitioners can compare the performance of different pipelines and choose the best approach for their specific use case.
case_studies.monetisation: The creation of EnterpriseDocBench presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and sell benchmarking and evaluation tools for document processing pipelines. Additionally, the framework can be used to develop more efficient and effective document processing pipelines, which can be sold as a product or service to enterprises.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models on robots is hindered by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. To address this, the authors propose a model-hardware co-characterization approach, evaluating model-hardware pairs under Cost, Energy, Time (CET) metrics. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more efficient than desktop-grade GPUs for VLA deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can build a cross-accelerator leaderboard to evaluate model-hardware pairs and identify the most suitable edge devices for their specific use case. By considering CET metrics, practitioners can optimize their VLA models for efficient on-robot deployment.
case_studies.monetisation: The research opens up opportunities for companies to develop and market specialized edge devices for VLA deployment, catering to the growing demand for efficient robot control systems. Additionally, the model-hardware co-characterization approach can be licensed or integrated into existing robotics platforms, providing a new revenue stream for companies operating in this space.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Computer Vision, NLP, MLOps

case_studies.title: HalluCiteChecker: A Lightweight Toolkit for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Verification in the Era of AI Scientists
case_studies.abstract: We introduce HalluCiteChecker, a toolkit for detecting and verifying hallucinated citations in scientific papers. While AI assistant technologies have transformed the academic writing process, including citation recommendation, they have also led to the emergence of hallucinated citations that do not correspond to any existing work. Such citations not only undermine the credibility of scientific papers but also impose an additional burden on reviewers and authors, who must manually verify their validity during the review process. In this study, we formalize hallucinated citation detection as a
case_studies.summary: The emergence of hallucinated citations in scientific papers, caused by AI assistant technologies, undermines the credibility of research and imposes a burden on reviewers and authors. HalluCiteChecker, a lightweight toolkit, addresses this issue by detecting and verifying hallucinated citations using a formalized approach. The outcome of this study is a potential solution to improve the validity and reliability of scientific citations.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from HalluCiteChecker by formalizing similar problems in their domain and developing toolkits to address them. By doing so, they can create practical solutions to real-world issues and improve the overall quality of research and publications.
case_studies.monetisation: The HalluCiteChecker toolkit presents a clear product opportunity, as academic institutions and research organizations may be willing to pay for a reliable solution to detect and verify hallucinated citations. A company can be built around this product, offering subscription-based services or licensing the technology to academic publishers and research institutions.

case_studies.title: Domain-Adapted Small Language Models for Reliable Clinical Triage
case_studies.abstract: Accurate and consistent Emergency Severity Index (ESI) assignment remains a persistent challenge in emergency departments, where highly variable free-text triage documentation contributes to mistriage and workflow inefficiencies. This study evaluates whether open-source small language models (SLMs) can serve as reliable, privacy-preserving decision-support tools for clinical triage. We systematically compared multiple SLMs across diverse prompting pipelines and found that clinical vignettes, concise summaries of triage narratives, yielded the most accurate predictions. The SLM, Qwen2.5-7B, dem
case_studies.summary: The Emergency Severity Index (ESI) assignment in emergency departments is a challenging task due to variable free-text triage documentation, leading to mistriage and workflow inefficiencies. This study evaluates the use of open-source small language models (SLMs) as reliable decision-support tools for clinical triage, finding that clinical vignettes yield the most accurate predictions. The SLM, Qwen2.5-7B, demonstrated promising results in this context.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by utilizing clinical vignettes as input to SLMs for clinical triage, which can improve the accuracy of ESI assignments. Additionally, practitioners can experiment with different prompting pipelines to optimize the performance of SLMs in their specific use cases.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of a clinical triage decision-support tool based on SLMs could provide a significant business opportunity, particularly if it can demonstrate improved patient outcomes and reduced healthcare costs. A company could be founded to commercialize this technology, offering it as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution to emergency departments and other healthcare providers.

case_studies.title: SynSur: An end-to-end generative pipeline for synthetic industrial surface defect generation and detection
case_studies.abstract: The bottleneck in learning-based industrial defect detection is often limited not by model capacity, but by the scarcity of labeled defect data: defects are rare, annotations are expensive, and collecting balanced training sets is slow. We present an end-to-end pipeline for synthetic defect generation and annotation, combining Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, mask-guided inpainting, and sample filtering with automatic label derivation, and demonstrates the potential of real data with realistic synthetic samples to overcome data scarcity. The evaluation is conducted
case_studies.summary: The scarcity of labeled defect data hinders the development of industrial defect detection models. To address this, the SynSur pipeline combines Vision-Language-Model-based prompts, LoRA-adapted diffusion, and mask-guided inpainting to generate synthetic defect data. This approach demonstrates the potential to overcome data scarcity and improve defect detection models with realistic synthetic samples.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by integrating Vision-Language-Model-based prompts and LoRA-adapted diffusion into their existing data generation pipelines to create more realistic and diverse synthetic data. By leveraging this pipeline, practitioners can reduce the need for manual annotation and accelerate the development of industrial defect detection models.
case_studies.monetisation: The SynSur pipeline presents a clear product opportunity for companies developing industrial defect detection systems, as it can help reduce the cost and time associated with data collection and annotation. By licensing or integrating this technology, companies can create more accurate and efficient defect detection models, leading to improved quality control and reduced maintenance costs.

case_studies.title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model Under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insufficiently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was used to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulatin
case_studies.summary: The study evaluates the robustness of a foundation segmentation model, specifically the Segment Anything Model (SAM), under simulated domain shifts in abdominal CT scans. The AI approach involves a systematic slice-level audit of SAM using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. The outcome highlights the need for further quantification of the model's robustness under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts, with implications for Health Digital Twin deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this study's findings, AI practitioners can use a standardized ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty in their own models. By doing so, they can systematically evaluate the robustness of their models under various domain shifts, leading to more reliable and generalizable performance.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings have significant monetisation potential, as they can inform the development of more robust and reliable medical imaging models, leading to improved patient outcomes and reduced healthcare costs. A potential business opportunity is to develop and market a software solution that integrates the SAM model with the standardized protocol, offering a more accurate and generalizable spleen segmentation tool for healthcare providers.

case_studies.title: Feasible-First Exploration for Constrained ML Deployment Optimization in Crash-Prone Hierarchical Search Spaces
case_studies.abstract: Deploying machine learning models under production constraints requires joint optimization over model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. This induces a hierarchical mixed-variable search space in which many configurations are invalid: evaluations may crash, exceed memory limits, or violate latency constraints. Standard black-box optimizers such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators (TPE) and constrained Bayesian optimization are effective when valid configurations are common, but they can spend a large fraction of a small evaluation budget on invalid or uni
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying machine learning models under production constraints is addressed, where the goal is to jointly optimize model family, quantization scheme, runtime backend, and serving configuration. The AI approach uses feasible-first exploration to navigate a hierarchical mixed-variable search space, avoiding invalid configurations that may crash or exceed memory limits. The outcome is an optimization method that can efficiently search for valid configurations, reducing the evaluation budget spent on invalid ones.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by incorporating feasible-first exploration into their optimization pipelines, particularly when dealing with constrained and hierarchical search spaces. This can be achieved by modifying existing black-box optimizers, such as Tree-structured Parzen Estimators, to prioritize feasible configurations and avoid wasting evaluations on invalid ones.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed optimization method can be monetized by developing a software product that helps machine learning teams efficiently deploy models under production constraints, reducing the time and cost associated with searching for valid configurations. This product can be targeted at companies that heavily rely on machine learning, such as tech giants, and can be sold as a subscription-based service or a one-time licensing fee.

case_studies.title: Network Impact of Post-Quantum Certificate Chain sizes on Time to First Byte in TLS Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) is a rapidly growing deployment challenge as cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQC) continue to advance, leaving traditional cryptographic algorithms used in X.509 vulnerable to attack. However, PQC introduces significant deployment challenges in real-world networks, with handshake sizes increasing from 5x to over 20x compared to classical algorithms. In this work, we evaluate the time to first byte (TTFB) under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning existing internet infrastructure to quantum-safe certificate s
case_studies.summary: The problem of transitioning to post-quantum cryptography in real-world networks is becoming increasingly pressing, with traditional cryptographic algorithms being vulnerable to quantum computer attacks. The authors' AI approach involves evaluating the time to first byte under CDN-focused TLS conditions to characterize the latency cost of transitioning to quantum-safe certificates. The outcome of this study provides valuable insights into the potential impact of post-quantum cryptography on network performance.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this research in practice, AI practitioners can use the findings to inform the design of more efficient post-quantum cryptographic protocols and deployment strategies. By considering the latency costs associated with post-quantum cryptography, practitioners can develop more effective solutions for securing internet infrastructure.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has concrete business opportunities in the development of quantum-safe security products and services, such as secure certificate issuance and management solutions. Companies can leverage the findings of this study to create more efficient and scalable post-quantum cryptographic solutions, addressing a growing need in the industry.

case_studies.title: MetaSR: Content-Adaptive Metadata Orchestration for Generative Super-Resolution
case_studies.abstract: We study generative super-resolution (SR) in real-world scenarios where content and degradations vary across domains, genres, and segments. For example, images and videos may alternate between text overlays, fast motion, smooth cartoons, and low-light faces, each benefiting from different forms of side information. Existing metadata-guided SR methods typically use a fixed conditioning design, which is suboptimal when useful cues are content dependent and transmission budgets are limited. We propose MetaSR, a Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based framework that selects and injects task-relevant met
case_studies.summary: The problem of generative super-resolution in real-world scenarios is addressed, where content and degradations vary across domains, genres, and segments. The proposed AI approach, MetaSR, utilizes a Diffusion Transformer-based framework to select and inject task-relevant metadata, adapting to content-dependent cues. The outcome is a more efficient and effective super-resolution method, potentially improving image and video quality in various applications.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the concept of content-adaptive metadata orchestration to their own generative models, allowing for more flexible and efficient processing of diverse data. By considering the specific requirements of each task and adapting the model accordingly, practitioners can improve the performance and robustness of their AI systems.
case_studies.monetisation: The MetaSR framework has clear potential for application in industries such as video production, gaming, and virtual reality, where high-quality image and video rendering is crucial. Companies can leverage this technology to develop more efficient and effective super-resolution tools, offering a competitive edge in the market and generating revenue through software sales or licensing.

case_studies.title: Apriori-based Analysis of Learned Helplessness in Mathematics Tutoring: Behavioral Patterns by Level, Intervention, and Outcome
case_studies.abstract: This study applied the Apriori algorithm to analyze behavioral interaction patterns associated with learned helplessness (LH) in mathematics tutoring system logs. Interaction data were examined across three dimensions: LH level (low vs. high), system-based intervention (with vs. without), and problem-solving outcomes (solved vs. unsolved). The analysis of the complete dataset showed that skipping problems without using hints was the most frequent pattern linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors such as not skipping were less dominant overall. Comparisons by LH level showed that
case_studies.summary: The study addresses the issue of learned helplessness in mathematics tutoring by analyzing interaction patterns in system logs. The Apriori algorithm is applied to identify behavioral patterns associated with learned helplessness, examining dimensions such as level, intervention, and outcome. The analysis reveals that skipping problems without using hints is the most frequent pattern linked to unsolved outcomes, while persistence behaviors are less dominant overall.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the insights from this study by integrating Apriori-based analysis into their own tutoring systems to identify and address learned helplessness. By leveraging this approach, practitioners can develop more effective interventions and support systems to improve student outcomes.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings can be monetized by developing and marketing AI-powered tutoring systems that incorporate learned helplessness detection and intervention capabilities. Companies can create adaptive learning platforms that use Apriori-based analysis to provide personalized support and improve student outcomes, generating revenue through subscription-based models or licensing agreements.

case_studies.title: Exploring the Potential of Probabilistic Transformer for Time Series Modeling: A Report on the ST-PT Framework
case_studies.abstract: The Probabilistic Transformer (PT) establishes that the Transformer's self-attention plus its feed-forward block is mathematically equivalent to Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). Under this equivalence the Transformer ceases to be a black-box neural network and becomes a programmable factor graph: graph topology, factor potentials, and the message-passing schedule are all explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. PT was originally developed for natural language and in this report we investigate its potential for time series. We first
case_studies.summary: The problem of time series modeling is addressed through the application of the Probabilistic Transformer (PT) framework, which establishes a mathematical equivalence between the Transformer's self-attention and Mean-Field Variational Inference (MFVI) on a Conditional Random Field (CRF). The PT approach allows for the Transformer to become a programmable factor graph, enabling explicit and inspectable primitives that can be engineered. The outcome of this investigation is a report on the potential of PT for time series modeling, exploring its capabilities and limitations in this domain.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the PT framework to time series modeling, practitioners should first understand the mathematical equivalence between the Transformer's self-attention and MFVI on a CRF, and then explore how to engineer the graph topology, factor potentials, and message-passing schedule to suit their specific use case. By leveraging the PT framework, practitioners can potentially create more transparent and interpretable time series models, which can be beneficial for various applications, such as forecasting and anomaly detection.
case_studies.monetisation: The PT framework has the potential to be monetized through the development of specialized time series modeling products or services, such as predictive maintenance or financial forecasting tools, which can leverage the framework's capabilities to provide more accurate and reliable results. Companies can adapt the PT framework to create tailored solutions for their clients, offering a competitive advantage in the market and generating revenue through licensing or subscription-based models.

case_studies.title: FutureWorld: A Live Environment for Training Predictive Agents with Real-World Outcome Rewards
case_studies.abstract: Live future prediction refers to the task of making predictions about real-world events before they unfold. This task is increasingly studied using large language model-based agent systems, and it is important for building agents that can continually learn from real-world. Just as interactive environments have often driven progress in agents, advancing live future prediction naturally motivates viewing it as a learning environment. Prior works have explored future prediction from several different parts, but have generally not framed it as a unified learning environment. This task is appealing
case_studies.summary: The problem of live future prediction involves making predictions about real-world events before they unfold, which can be addressed using large language model-based agent systems. The proposed AI approach, FutureWorld, frames live future prediction as a unified learning environment to train predictive agents with real-world outcome rewards. The outcome of this approach is a potentially powerful tool for building agents that can continually learn from the real world.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on designing interactive environments that simulate real-world scenarios, allowing agents to learn from their predictions and adapt to new situations. By using real-world outcome rewards, practitioners can encourage agents to develop more accurate and effective prediction strategies.
case_studies.monetisation: The FutureWorld approach has potential business applications in areas such as predictive maintenance, financial forecasting, and risk management, where accurate predictions can drive significant revenue and cost savings. Companies can leverage this technology to develop innovative products and services that provide actionable insights and predictions to their customers.

case_studies.title: Deep-testing: the case of dependence detection
case_studies.abstract: Deep learning methods have proved highly effective for classification and image recognition problems. In this paper, we ask whether this success can be transferred to hypothesis testing: if a neural network can distinguish, for example, an image of a handwritten digit from another, can it also distinguish an "image of a sample" (such as a scatter plot) generated under a given statistical model from one generated outside that model? Motivated by this idea, we propose a novel procedure called deep-testing, which approaches the classical inferential problem of hypothesis testing through deep lear
case_studies.summary: The problem of hypothesis testing in statistical models is addressed through a novel approach called deep-testing. This approach utilizes deep learning methods to distinguish between samples generated under a given statistical model and those generated outside of it. The outcome of this research is a proposed procedure for deep-testing, which has the potential to revolutionize the field of hypothesis testing.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can use neural networks to analyze scatter plots and other visual representations of data to determine whether they are generated under a specific statistical model. By leveraging deep learning methods, practitioners can develop more accurate and efficient hypothesis testing procedures.
case_studies.monetisation: The deep-testing approach has the potential to be monetized through the development of software tools or consulting services that help organizations apply this method to their data analysis needs. Companies that specialize in data analytics or statistical modeling could leverage this research to create new products or services that improve hypothesis testing capabilities.

case_studies.title: Culturally Aware GenAI Risks for Youth: Perspectives from Youth, Parents, and Teachers in a Non-Western Context
case_studies.abstract: Generative AI tools are widely used by youth and have introduced new privacy and safety challenges. While prior research has explored youth's safety in GenAI within western context, it often overlooks the cultural, religious, and social dimensions of technology use that strongly shape youths digital experiences in countries like Saudi Arabia. To address the gap, this study explores children (aged 7 to 17), parents and teachers interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions through non-western lens. Through a mixed methods approach, we analyzed 736 Reddit and 1,262 X(Twitter) posts and cond
case_studies.summary: The widespread use of generative AI tools by youth has introduced new privacy and safety challenges, particularly in non-western contexts where cultural and social dimensions of technology use are distinct. This study used a mixed methods approach to analyze interactions with GenAI tools and risk perceptions among children, parents, and teachers in Saudi Arabia. The findings highlight the need for culturally aware GenAI risks assessments and mitigation strategies to ensure safe technology use among youth in diverse contexts.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the cultural and social contexts of their target users when designing and deploying GenAI tools. This includes incorporating diverse perspectives and risk assessments to ensure that their tools are safe and effective for users from varying backgrounds.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's focus on culturally aware GenAI risks presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI tools that cater to diverse cultural and social contexts, addressing a gap in the current market. By developing GenAI tools that prioritize safety and cultural sensitivity, companies can tap into the growing demand for responsible and inclusive AI solutions.

case_studies.title: Calibrated Surprise: An Information-Theoretic Account of Creative Quality
case_studies.abstract: The essence of good creative writing is calibrated surprise: when constraints from all relevant dimensions act together, the feasible solution space collapses into a narrow region, and the surviving choices look least predictable from an unconstrained view. "Calibrated" has a precise meaning: the author's intent, the reader's reasonable expectation, and the logic of reality converge. When these three independent judgements agree on every dimension, the set of admissible writing choices is forced into a very small region. A mathematical corollary follows: full-dimensional accuracy and mediocrit
case_studies.summary: The problem of evaluating creative writing quality is addressed through the concept of calibrated surprise, where constraints from multiple dimensions converge to produce a narrow set of feasible solutions. The AI approach involves using information-theoretic principles to quantify the predictability of writing choices. The outcome is a mathematical framework for understanding the essence of good creative writing, with potential applications in natural language processing and generation.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this concept by incorporating multi-dimensional constraints into their language generation models to produce more surprises and engaging text. By quantifying the predictability of writing choices, practitioners can develop more sophisticated evaluation metrics for creative writing quality.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop an AI-powered writing assistant that uses the calibrated surprise framework to provide feedback and suggestions to writers, helping them to improve the quality and creativity of their work. This could be marketed as a tool for professional writers, students, and language learners, with potential applications in education, publishing, and content creation.

case_studies.title: Scalable Inference Architectures for Compound AI Systems: A Production Deployment Study
case_studies.abstract: Modern enterprise AI applications increasingly rely on compound AI systems - architectures that compose multiple models, retrievers, and tools to accomplish complex tasks. Deploying such systems in production demands inference infrastructure that can efficiently serve concurrent, heterogeneous model invocations while maintaining cost-effectiveness and low latency. This paper presents a production deployment study of a modular, platform-agnostic inference architecture developed at Salesforce to support compound AI use cases including Agentforce (autonomous AI agents) and ApexGuru (AI-powered co
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying compound AI systems in production environments is addressed through the development of a modular, platform-agnostic inference architecture. The AI approach involves composing multiple models, retrievers, and tools to accomplish complex tasks, with a focus on efficient inference infrastructure. The outcome is a scalable and cost-effective solution that can support concurrent, heterogeneous model invocations with low latency.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by designing modular inference architectures that can efficiently serve concurrent model invocations, and by leveraging platform-agnostic solutions to support heterogeneous models. By doing so, they can improve the scalability and cost-effectiveness of their compound AI systems, enabling wider adoption in production environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The developed inference architecture presents a clear product opportunity, particularly in the context of enterprise AI applications, where compound AI systems are increasingly being used to drive business value. Companies can leverage this technology to develop and deploy scalable AI solutions, generating revenue through subscription-based models or AI-powered services.

case_studies.title: MAIC-UI: Making Interactive Courseware with Generative UI
case_studies.abstract: Creating interactive STEM courseware traditionally requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. While generative AI can produce HTML codes, existing tools generate static presentations rather than interactive simulations, struggle with long documents, and lack pedagogical accuracy mechanisms. Furthermore, full regeneration for modifications requires 200--600 seconds, disrupting creative flow. We present MAIC-UI, a zero-code authoring system that enables educators to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. MAIC-UI employs: (1) st
case_studies.summary: The traditional process of creating interactive STEM courseware is time-consuming and requires HTML/CSS/JavaScript expertise, leaving barriers for educators. MAIC-UI addresses this issue by employing a zero-code authoring system that utilizes generative AI to create and rapidly edit interactive courseware from textbooks, PPTs, and PDFs. This approach enables educators to create interactive simulations without requiring extensive coding knowledge, resulting in increased efficiency and pedagogical accuracy.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this AI approach, practitioners can focus on developing zero-code authoring systems that integrate generative AI capabilities, allowing users to create interactive content without requiring extensive coding expertise. By streamlining the content creation process, practitioners can increase efficiency and accessibility for educators and learners alike.
case_studies.monetisation: The MAIC-UI system presents a clear product opportunity for companies specializing in educational technology, as it can be integrated into existing learning management systems or offered as a standalone tool for educators. By licensing or commercializing the MAIC-UI technology, companies can capitalize on the growing demand for interactive and engaging educational content.

case_studies.title: RESTestBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating the Effectiveness of LLM-Generated REST API Test Cases from NL Requirements
case_studies.abstract: Existing REST API testing tools are typically evaluated using code coverage and crash-based fault metrics. However, recent LLM-based approaches increasingly generate tests from NL requirements to validate functional behaviour, making traditional metrics weak proxies for whether generated tests validate intended behaviour. To address this gap, we present RESTestBench, a benchmark comprising three REST services paired with manually verified NL requirements in both precise and vague variants, enabling controlled and reproducible evaluation of requirement-based test generation. RESTestBench furthe
case_studies.summary: The existing REST API testing tools are limited in their ability to evaluate the effectiveness of tests generated from natural language requirements. To address this, the authors propose RESTestBench, a benchmark for evaluating the effectiveness of LLM-generated REST API test cases from NL requirements. The outcome is a controlled and reproducible evaluation of requirement-based test generation, enabling a more accurate assessment of test effectiveness.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by using RESTestBench to evaluate the effectiveness of their own LLM-generated test cases, allowing them to refine and improve their testing approaches. By leveraging this benchmark, practitioners can ensure that their tests accurately validate the intended behavior of their REST APIs.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of RESTestBench presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in API testing and validation, as it provides a standardized framework for evaluating the effectiveness of LLM-generated test cases. By integrating RESTestBench into their testing suites, these companies can offer more comprehensive and accurate testing solutions to their clients, thereby increasing their competitive edge and potential revenue streams.

case_studies.title: TrialCalibre: A Fully Automated Causal Engine for RCT Benchmarking and Observational Trial Calibration
case_studies.abstract: Real-world evidence (RWE) studies that emulate target trials increasingly inform regulatory and clinical decisions, yet residual, hard-to-quantify biases still limit their credibility. The recently proposed BenchExCal framework addresses this challenge via a two-stage Benchmark, Expand, Calibrate process, which first compares an observational emulation against an existing randomized controlled trial (RCT), then uses observed divergence to calibrate a second emulation for a new indication causal effect estimation. While methodologically powerful, BenchExCal is resource intensive and difficult t
case_studies.summary: The problem of residual biases in real-world evidence studies is addressed through the development of TrialCalibre, a fully automated causal engine. The AI approach involves a two-stage process of benchmarking and calibration to improve the credibility of observational trial emulations. The outcome is a more robust method for estimating causal effects in new indications, increasing the reliability of real-world evidence studies.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by identifying areas where observational data can be calibrated against randomized controlled trials, and then using the resulting insights to inform decision-making. By leveraging the TrialCalibre engine, researchers can streamline the process of benchmarking and calibration, making it more efficient and scalable.
case_studies.monetisation: The TrialCalibre engine has the potential to be developed into a commercial product, offering a solution for pharmaceutical companies and research institutions seeking to improve the validity of their real-world evidence studies. By licensing or partnering with companies that specialize in healthcare data analytics, the authors may be able to generate revenue from their innovation.

case_studies.title: Conditional misalignment: common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers
case_studies.abstract: Finetuning a language model can lead to emergent misalignment (EM) [Betley et al., 2025b]. Models trained on a narrow distribution of misaligned behavior generalize to more egregious behaviors when tested outside the training distribution. We study a set of interventions proposed to reduce EM. We confirm that these interventions reduce or eliminate EM on existing evaluations (questions like "How do I make a quick buck?"). However, if the evaluation prompts are tweaked to resemble the training context, the model displays EM. We call this conditional misalignment. As in standard EM, the model di
case_studies.summary: The problem of emergent misalignment in language models can lead to undesirable behaviors when tested outside the training distribution. The authors propose a study on conditional misalignment, where common interventions can hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers. The outcome of the study reveals that even with interventions, language models can still display emergent misalignment when evaluated with prompts that resemble the training context.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners should be cautious when evaluating language models and consider the potential for conditional misalignment, using a variety of evaluation prompts to uncover hidden biases. By acknowledging the limitations of current interventions, practitioners can develop more robust testing methods to ensure the safety and reliability of language models.
case_studies.monetisation: The findings of this study could be used to develop more robust language models for commercial applications, such as chatbots or virtual assistants, where safety and reliability are paramount. A company could leverage this research to create a product that specializes in testing and evaluating language models for conditional misalignment, providing a valuable service to organizations looking to deploy AI safely.

case_studies.title: Does social identity matter in software engineering? Assessing the case of research software engineers
case_studies.abstract: Social identity is a concept from psychology that refers to the part of an individual's identity that derives from their group membership(s). In this paper, we explore social identity in members of the professional community of Research Software Engineers (RSEs). Using a mixed-methods approach, our study combined computational linguistic analysis and inferential statistics to examine over 28,000 social media posts, 1,700 blogs, and survey responses from 381 professional RSEs. The findings highlight the emergence of a collective RSE identity and demonstrate its role in shaping professional well
case_studies.summary: The study explores the concept of social identity in Research Software Engineers (RSEs) and its impact on their professional well-being. The AI approach used a mixed-methods methodology, combining computational linguistic analysis and inferential statistics to analyze social media posts, blogs, and survey responses. The outcome highlights the emergence of a collective RSE identity and its role in shaping professional well-being.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the findings of this study by recognizing the importance of social identity in professional communities and using similar methodologies to analyze and understand the dynamics of their own communities. By doing so, they can develop more effective strategies for building and maintaining a strong sense of community and identity among their team members.
case_studies.monetisation: The study's findings on social identity in RSEs could be monetized by developing targeted training programs or community-building initiatives that cater to the specific needs and interests of RSEs. Companies could also use the insights from this study to create more effective recruitment and retention strategies for RSEs, which could lead to increased revenue and competitiveness in the industry.

case_studies.title: Leveraging LLMs for Multi-File DSL Code Generation: An Industrial Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform strongly on general-purpose code generation, yet their applicability to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) remains underexplored, especially for repository-scale change generation spanning multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language (NL) instruction. We report an industrial case study at BMW that adapts code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL that drives downstream Java/TypeScript code generation. We develop an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction, multi-file task r
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this case study is the applicability of large language models (LLMs) to enterprise domain-specific languages (DSLs) for code generation. The AI approach involves adapting code-oriented LLMs to generate and modify project-root DSL artifacts for an Xtext-based DSL. The outcome is an end-to-end pipeline for dataset construction and multi-file task generation from a single natural-language instruction, as demonstrated in an industrial case study at BMW.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can develop similar pipelines for their own DSLs by leveraging code-oriented LLMs and constructing datasets tailored to their specific use cases. They can also experiment with adapting LLMs to generate code for multiple files and folder structures from a single natural-language instruction.
case_studies.monetisation: The monetisation potential of this approach lies in its ability to streamline code generation and modification for enterprises, reducing manual labor and increasing efficiency. A concrete business opportunity could be to develop a product or service that provides tailored LLM-based code generation solutions for companies using domain-specific languages.

case_studies.title: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Models across XPUs: Constraints and Acceleration for On-Robot Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are promising for generalist robot control, but on-robot deployment is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. Most prior evaluations rely on desktop-grade GPUs, obscuring the trade-offs and opportunities offered by heterogeneous edge accelerators (GPUs/XPUs/NPUs). We present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization. First, we build a cross-accelerator leaderboard and evaluate model-hardware pairs under CET (Cost, Energy, Time), showing that right-sized edge devices can be more
case_studies.summary: The problem of deploying Vision-Language-Action models on robots is bottlenecked by real-time inference under tight cost and energy budgets. To address this, the authors present a systematic analysis for low-cost VLA deployment via model-hardware co-characterization, evaluating model-hardware pairs under cost, energy, and time constraints. The outcome shows that right-sized edge devices can be more effective than desktop-grade GPUs for on-robot deployment.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the lessons from this study by considering the trade-offs between different edge accelerators and selecting the most suitable one for their specific use case. By characterizing the constraints and opportunities of their model-hardware pairs, practitioners can optimize their deployments for better performance and efficiency.
case_studies.monetisation: The research has a clear product opportunity in the field of robotics, particularly in areas where real-time inference and low-cost deployment are crucial, such as warehouse automation or service robotics. Companies can leverage the findings of this study to develop optimized Vision-Language-Action models and edge devices for on-robot deployment, creating new business opportunities in the robotics and automation sectors.
case_studies.relevance_tag: AI Agents, Computer Vision, NLP, MLOps, Automation

case_studies.title: On-Device Vision Training, Deployment, and Inference on a Thumb-Sized Microcontroller
case_studies.abstract: This paper presents a complete, end-to-end on-device vision machine learning pipeline, comprising data acquisition, two-layer CNN training with Adam optimization, and real-time inference, executing entirely on a microcontroller-class device costing $15-40 USD. Unlike cloud-based workflows that require external infrastructure and conceal the computational pipeline from the practitioner, this system implements every step of the core ML lifecycle in approximately 1,750 lines of readable C++ that compiles in under one minute using the Arduino IDE, with no external ML dependencies. Running on the S
case_studies.summary: The problem of relying on cloud-based workflows for machine learning tasks is addressed by developing an on-device vision machine learning pipeline. The AI approach involves using a two-layer CNN with Adam optimization, trained and deployed on a microcontroller-class device. The outcome is a complete, end-to-end vision machine learning pipeline that can run in real-time on a low-cost device.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this approach by leveraging microcontroller-class devices to develop edge-based machine learning solutions, reducing reliance on cloud infrastructure. This can be achieved by using frameworks like Arduino IDE to compile and deploy machine learning models on low-cost devices.
case_studies.monetisation: The development of on-device vision machine learning pipelines can be monetized by creating products that utilize edge-based computer vision, such as smart home devices or industrial automation systems. Companies can also offer services to develop custom on-device machine learning solutions for clients, providing a new revenue stream.

case_studies.title: A Deployable Embodied Vision-Language Navigation System with Hierarchical Cognition and Context-Aware Exploration
case_studies.abstract: Bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment remains a key challenge in intelligent robotic systems, where perception, reasoning, and planning must operate under strict constraints on computation, memory, energy, and real-time execution. In vision-language navigation (VLN), existing approaches often face a fundamental trade-off between strong reasoning capabilities and efficient deployment on real-world platforms. In this paper, we present a deployable embodied VLN system that achieves both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning on real-world robotic platform
case_studies.summary: The problem of bridging the gap between embodied intelligence and embedded deployment in intelligent robotic systems is addressed through a vision-language navigation system. The AI approach involves hierarchical cognition and context-aware exploration to achieve both high efficiency and robust high-level reasoning. The outcome is a deployable embodied vision-language navigation system that can operate on real-world robotic platforms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can focus on developing hierarchical cognitive models that balance strong reasoning capabilities with efficient deployment on real-world platforms. By integrating context-aware exploration, practitioners can improve the robustness and adaptability of their AI systems in dynamic environments.
case_studies.monetisation: The developed system has a concrete business opportunity in the robotics and autonomous systems industry, where efficient and robust navigation systems are in high demand. Companies can adapt and license this technology to enhance their robotic products, such as service robots, drones, or self-driving cars, and create new revenue streams.

case_studies.title: Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Industrial robotic manipulation demands reliable long-horizon execution across embodiments, tasks, and changing object distributions. While Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong generalization, they remain fundamentally reactive. By optimizing the next action given the current observation without evaluating potential futures, they are brittle to the compounding failure modes of long-horizon tasks. Cortex 2.0 shifts from reactive control to plan-and-act by generating candidate future trajectories in visual latent space, scoring them for expected success and efficiency, then com
case_studies.summary: Industrial robotic manipulation requires reliable long-horizon execution, but current Vision-Language-Action models are reactive and prone to failure. Cortex 2.0 addresses this by shifting to a plan-and-act approach, generating candidate future trajectories and scoring them for success and efficiency. This approach enables more robust and efficient execution of industrial robotic tasks.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can focus on developing models that generate and evaluate potential future trajectories, rather than just reacting to current observations. By incorporating planning and evaluation into their models, practitioners can create more robust and efficient AI systems for industrial robotic manipulation.
case_studies.monetisation: The Cortex 2.0 approach presents a clear business opportunity for companies developing industrial robotic systems, as it enables more efficient and reliable execution of tasks. By integrating this technology into their products, companies can differentiate themselves and attract customers seeking more robust and efficient industrial robotic solutions.

case_studies.title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
case_studies.abstract: The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM), maintained by the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) collaboration, enabled the harmonisation of electronic health records data of nearly one billion patients in 83 countries. Yet generating real-world evidence (RWE) from these repositories remains a manual process requiring clinical, epidemiological and technical expertise. LLMs and multi-agent systems have shown promise for clinical tasks, but RWE automation exposes a fundamental challenge: agentic systems introduce emergent behaviours, coord
case_studies.summary: The generation of real-world evidence from large health record datasets is a manual process that requires significant expertise, limiting its scalability and efficiency. The proposed FastOMOP architecture utilizes AI and multi-agent systems to automate this process, leveraging the OMOP Common Data Model to harmonize data from diverse sources. By automating real-world evidence generation, FastOMOP aims to improve the speed and reliability of clinical research and decision-making.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the principles of FastOMOP, AI practitioners should focus on developing architectures that integrate multiple AI systems and data models to automate complex tasks, such as real-world evidence generation. By leveraging existing data standards like OMOP CDM, practitioners can ensure interoperability and facilitate the adoption of their solutions in real-world settings.
case_studies.monetisation: The FastOMOP architecture presents a concrete business opportunity for companies specializing in healthcare data analytics and clinical research, as it offers a scalable and efficient solution for generating real-world evidence. By commercializing FastOMOP or similar architectures, businesses can provide valuable services to pharmaceutical companies, research institutions, and healthcare providers, helping them make data-driven decisions and improve patient outcomes.
case_studies.relevance_tag: Healthcare AI, Automation, AI Agents, LLMs

case_studies.title: AgentPulse: A Continuous Multi-Signal Framework for Evaluating AI Agents in Deployment
case_studies.abstract: Static benchmarks measure what AI agents can do at a fixed point in time but not how they are adopted, maintained, or experienced in deployment. We introduce AgentPulse, a continuous evaluation framework scoring 50 agents across 10 workload categories along four factors (Benchmark Performance, Adoption Signals, Community Sentiment, and Ecosystem Health) aggregated from 18 real-time signals across GitHub, package registries, IDE marketplaces, social platforms, and benchmark leaderboards. Three analyses ground the framework. The four factors capture largely complementary information (n=50; $ρ_{\
case_studies.summary: The evaluation of AI agents is limited by static benchmarks that do not account for real-world deployment and user experience. The proposed AgentPulse framework addresses this by introducing a continuous evaluation methodology that assesses AI agents across multiple factors and signals. The framework demonstrates its effectiveness through analyses of 50 agents across 10 workload categories, providing a more comprehensive understanding of AI agent performance and adoption.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this framework, AI practitioners can integrate AgentPulse into their development workflows to monitor and evaluate their AI agents' performance and adoption in real-time. By using a multi-signal approach, practitioners can identify areas for improvement and optimize their AI agents for better deployment and user experience.
case_studies.monetisation: The AgentPulse framework presents a business opportunity for companies to develop and market AI evaluation and monitoring tools that help organizations optimize their AI deployments. By providing a comprehensive and continuous evaluation methodology, companies can offer valuable insights and services to AI developers and users, generating revenue through software sales, subscriptions, or consulting services.

case_studies.title: GradMAP: Gradient-Based Multi-Agent Proximal Learning for Grid-Edge Flexibility
case_studies.abstract: Coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices requires learning methods that remain fully decentralised in deployment while still respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics. This paper proposes gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning (GradMAP) to address this challenge. GradMAP trains independent neural-network policies for each agent without any parameter sharing, and each agent uses only its own local observation for online decision-making without communication. During offline training, GradMAP embeds a differentiable three-phase AC power-flow model in a primal-dual le
case_studies.summary: The problem of coordinating large populations of grid-edge devices in a decentralised manner while respecting three-phase AC distribution-network physics is addressed in this paper. The proposed AI approach, GradMAP, uses gradient-based multi-agent proximal learning to train independent neural-network policies for each agent. The outcome of this approach is a decentralised learning method that enables online decision-making without communication among agents.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this approach, AI practitioners can utilise the GradMAP framework to develop decentralised learning methods for other complex systems. By embedding differentiable models into a primal-dual learning framework, practitioners can enable independent agents to learn and make decisions in a decentralised manner.
case_studies.monetisation: The GradMAP approach has potential for monetisation in the energy sector, particularly in the development of smart grid technologies. Companies can utilise this approach to create products that enable decentralised coordination of grid-edge devices, leading to improved efficiency and reliability in energy distribution.

case_studies.title: Large-scale wireless network management via Open-RAN Tandem Apps: Cell on/off switching use case
case_studies.abstract: With growing mobile-network complexity, management and optimization have become increasingly difficult. Centralized algorithms face high control-data overhead and computational load, while distributed approaches often perform far from optimally. The O-RAN architecture introduces two tiers of RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling hierarchical network-management schemes. This work proposes Tandem Apps: a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both controllers. We show how to design Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve an agile, low-comp
case_studies.summary: The growing complexity of mobile networks has made management and optimization increasingly difficult, with centralized algorithms facing high control-data overhead and distributed approaches often performing suboptimally. This work proposes Tandem Apps, a pair of tightly coupled optimization mechanisms running on both RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs) in the O-RAN architecture, to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. The proposed approach enables hierarchical network-management schemes, but its practical implementation and outcome are still theoretical.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply this concept, AI practitioners can explore the design of Tandem Apps through architectural and functional splitting to achieve agile and low-complexity network management. By leveraging the O-RAN architecture and RICs, practitioners can develop hierarchical network-management schemes that address the limitations of centralized and distributed approaches.
case_studies.monetisation: The proposed Tandem Apps concept has monetisation potential as it can be adapted to various network management scenarios, offering a clear product opportunity for companies specializing in network optimization and management solutions. By developing and refining this concept, companies can create tailored products and services that address the growing need for efficient and scalable network management solutions.

case_studies.title: Diffusion Templates: A Unified Plugin Framework for Controllable Diffusion
case_studies.abstract: Controllable diffusion methods have substantially expanded the practical utility of diffusion models, but they are typically developed as isolated, backbone-specific systems with incompatible training pipelines, parameter formats, and runtime hooks. This fragmentation makes it difficult to reuse infrastructure across tasks, transfer capabilities across backbones, or compose multiple controls within a single generation pipeline. We present Diffusion Templates, a unified and open plugin framework that decouples base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The framework is organiz
case_studies.summary: The problem of fragmentation in controllable diffusion methods is addressed by decoupling base-model inference from controllable capability injection. The AI approach, known as Diffusion Templates, provides a unified and open plugin framework for integrating various controllable diffusion methods. This framework allows for greater flexibility and reusability of infrastructure across tasks, enabling the composition of multiple controls within a single generation pipeline.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply this framework by developing plugins for specific controllable diffusion methods, allowing for seamless integration with existing base models. By doing so, they can create more flexible and reusable generation pipelines, facilitating the transfer of capabilities across different backbone models.
case_studies.monetisation: The Diffusion Templates framework presents a concrete business opportunity for companies developing AI-powered generative models, as it enables the creation of more versatile and adaptable models. By licensing or integrating this framework, businesses can accelerate their development of controllable diffusion methods, providing a competitive edge in applications such as image and video generation, music synthesis, and text-to-speech systems.

case_studies.title: Joint Sato-Tate Laws for Transformations of Hecke Eigenvalues: The Vertical Case
case_studies.abstract: We introduce a framework within which a large class of joint equidistribution problems can be studied and resolved with effective error terms. This involves proving a higher dimensional and $μ$-analogue of the Erdös-Turán inequality, and utilizing the theory of the Hardy-Krause (H-K) variation from analysis, where, in particular, we formulate a technique to approximate a broad class of relevant functions by functions of bounded H-K variation. Our main focus will be on the vertical Sato-Tate problem for spaces of cusp forms and for families of elliptic curves over finite fields. In particular,
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the joint equidistribution of Hecke eigenvalues for cusp forms and elliptic curves over finite fields. The AI approach involves utilizing the theory of Hardy-Krause variation and formulating a technique to approximate relevant functions. The outcome is a framework for studying and resolving a large class of joint equidistribution problems with effective error terms.
case_studies.how_to_apply: AI practitioners can apply the technique of approximating functions of bounded Hardy-Krause variation to other problems in number theory and analysis. This approach can be used to resolve equidistribution problems in various mathematical contexts, providing a powerful tool for analyzing complex systems.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity is to develop software that utilizes this framework to analyze and optimize mathematical models in fields such as cryptography and coding theory. Companies specializing in mathematical modeling and analysis can leverage this research to create innovative products and services.

case_studies.title: Learning to Think from Multiple Thinkers
case_studies.abstract: We study learning with Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, all of whom provide correct but possibly systematically different solutions, e.g., step-by-step solutions to math problems written by different thinkers, or step-by-step execution traces of different programs solving the same problem. We consider classes that are computationally easy to learn using CoT supervision from a single thinker, but hard to learn with only end-result supervision, i.e., without CoT (Joshi et al. 2025). We establish that, under cryptographic assumptions, learning can be hard from CoT superv
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the difficulty of learning from Chain-of-Thought (CoT) supervision from multiple thinkers, which can provide correct but systematically different solutions. The AI approach involves learning with CoT supervision from multiple thinkers, analyzing the impact of cryptographic assumptions on the learning process. The outcome of this study establishes the hardness of learning from CoT supervision under certain assumptions, providing insights into the limitations of CoT learning.
case_studies.how_to_apply: To apply the findings of this study, AI practitioners should consider the potential biases and limitations of CoT supervision from multiple thinkers when designing and training AI models. This can involve carefully evaluating the consistency and quality of the supervision data to ensure that the model learns effectively and generalizes well to new situations.
case_studies.monetisation: A potential business opportunity arising from this study is the development of AI models that can effectively learn from diverse and potentially biased supervision data, which could be applied in areas such as education or decision support systems. By addressing the challenges of CoT learning from multiple thinkers, companies can create more robust and reliable AI solutions that can handle complex and nuanced tasks.

case_studies.title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed, yet their outputs can be highly sensitive to routine, non-adversarial variation in how users phrase queries, a gap not well addressed by existing red-teaming efforts. We propose Green Shielding, a user-centric agenda for building evidence-backed deployment guidance by characterizing how benign input variation shifts model behavior. We operationalize this agenda through the CUE criteria: benchmarks with authentic Context, reference standards and metrics that capture true Utility, and perturbations that reflect realistic variations in the E
case_studies.summary: The problem addressed in this study is the sensitivity of large language models to variations in user input, which can lead to inconsistent and potentially misleading results. The proposed approach, Green Shielding, is a user-centric agenda that characterizes how benign input variation shifts model behavior through the CUE criteria. The outcome of this approach is the development of evidence-backed deployment guidance for building trustworthy AI models.
